title: Autograph letter signed, Weymouth, 16 July 1799
text: Dr. Cotton Tufts writes from Weymouth to Rev. Stephen Peabody, settling money held in trust for Mrs. Peabody: he has left forty-five dollars and sixty cents “with the President’s Lady” (Abigail Adams) for the sums due and for the last quarter’s rent on the Medford farm. Elizabeth (Smith) Shaw Peabody was Abigail’s sister and Rev. Peabody’s wife. The catalogue gives Tufts’s birth year as 1734; this site follows 1732. Sold at iCollector, 25 October 2007, for $140 plus buyer’s premium.

title: Autograph letter signed to Dr. Philip Draper, Weymouth, 26 October 1785
text: The sheet behind the 1785 Draper letter described under Letters and Papers at Auction. Tufts declines an invitation to an association of physicians and asks how the society has proceeded. It was offered by University Archives on 6 December 2016 (estimate $800–$1,000) and is marked as having passed.
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: University Archives lot page

title: Abington selectmen and committee of correspondence to Cotton Tufts at Weymouth, 1 June 1775
text: A folded letter carried privately and addressed to Tufts as chairman of the committees of Cohasset, Hingham, Weymouth and Braintree. It begins “Pursuant to your letter (of the 30 of May)…” and is attested by Daniel Noyes, clerk, for the Abington selectmen and committee of correspondence, two weeks before Bunker Hill. It is addressed to him, not written by him. Offered by Schuyler Rumsey Philatelic Auctions, Sale 55, lot 349 (estimate $3,000–$4,000; opening bid $2,900). No lot photograph is shown.
label: Rumsey lot page
flag: The realized price of the Abington letter, and whether it sold, has not been found on a public page. Note: Pending further work.

title: Deed signed by John and Abigail Adams, 9 April 1803
text: A printed form completed in John Adams’s hand and signed by John and Abigail Adams, recording the sale of land at Braintree to Cotton Tufts Jr. Bonhams explains that Norton Quincy (1716–1801), Abigail’s uncle, left no children, so his lands passed to her, and calls the purchaser a cousin of Abigail. The document is in the Adamses’ names; Tufts is the grantee. Sold at Bonhams, New York, 21 November 2023 (sale 28447, lot 57), for $8,320 including premium.
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: Bonhams lot page

title: Town of Weymouth receipt, 19 February 1833
text: The Town of Weymouth bought 15⅞ pounds of butter “of Tufts & Whitten” for $2.54, and payment was received for the firm by a hand the listing reads as J. Byron. Cotton Tufts Jr. died at Weymouth later in 1833, so he was living when the receipt was written; the hand is not his. The sheet is offered on eBay (asking $59.77 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 206598016754
flag: The firm is written “Tufts & Whitten,” not Tufts & Whittemore, the name on this page; that they are the same Weymouth store is an inference from the name and the town, and the receipt does not name Cotton Tufts Jr. Note: Pending further work.

title: A 1766 Newburyport document offered as an “indenture,” Samuel Resnick to Samuel Tufts
text: A dealer listing mirrors an eBay sale of a document titled “1766 antique COLONIAL INDENTURE newburyport ma Samuel RESNICK to Samuel TUFTS,” asking $395 when it was last seen (28 November 2026). The names, the town and the year are those of the July 1766 notice shown on Samuel Tufts (several men). No photograph is shown here.
who: Josephmarc.com listing (mirror of an eBay sale)
label: Josephmarc listing
flag: Unverified. The listing page could not be opened, so its text, date, photographs and sale status are unconfirmed. It has not been established whether it is the same notice already shown on this site, a second notice, or a later sale of the first, and a February 1766 date reported for it has not been confirmed. Whether the writer is Dr. Samuel Tufts (1735–1799), rather than another Samuel Tufts, rests only on the name and place. Note: Pending further work.

title: Charlestown tax assessors’ account books, 1780–1782
text: Ten small octavo account books of Charlestown real-estate and poll taxes, signed by “various Charlestown tax assessors, including Sam Swan, Timothy Tufts, and others,” were sold at Skinner, Boston, on 11 November 2019 (sale 3311T, lot 1023) for $923.75, against an estimate of $300–$400. Edward C. Booth records that Timothy Tufts (1735–1805) was a selectman of Charlestown for most of the years between 1780 and 1792 (“The Tufts Family in Somerville,” Historic Leaves, vol. 1, p. 25). No lot photograph is shown.
label: Skinner lot page
flag: Unverified. The lot names only “Timothy Tufts.” Charlestown had other men of that name in 1780–1782, among them this man’s son Timothy (b. 1762), and the books have not been seen. Attaching the signature to Timothy Tufts (1735–1805) rests on his public office. Note: Pending further work.

title: T. Tufts & Co. letterhead, Alstead, N.H., 1873
text: A letter on the printed heading of T. Tufts & Co., Dry and Fancy Goods, Hats, Caps, Clothing, Boots and Shoes, dated at Alstead in 1873. The listing places it at “Alstead NY,” but the heading reads N.H. It is offered on eBay (asking $19.50 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 335676096203
flag: The heading gives only “T. Tufts & Co.” Attaching it to Timothy Tufts rests on the trade, the town, and Hurd’s statement that he conducted the Alstead business alone from 1851; the writer of the letter has not been identified. Note: Pending further work.

title: Auditor’s certificate, Virginia City, 18 May 1868
text: An auditor’s certificate of Montana Territory, dated at Virginia City on 18 May 1868, certifies that “James Tufts” had deposited territorial warrants with the Auditor, who was authorized to issue bonds for the sum. Tufts was then Secretary of the Territory. The certificate sold on eBay on 6 September 2026 for $29.99.
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 307166462503
flag: The certificate names only “James Tufts.” That he is the Territorial Secretary rests on the name, the town (then the territorial capital) and the year. Note: Pending further work.

title: Letter from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology to Prof. J. Tufts, Exeter, N.H., 21 September 1889
text: James P. Munroe, writing on Institute of Technology paper, tells the Exeter teacher that the faculty has voted to give a student, Mr. Bowers, credit for four subjects passed in the June examinations and to admit him if he passes the rest in June or September 1890. The letter is addressed to “Prof. J. Tufts, Exeter, N.H.” It is offered on eBay (asking $180.50 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 206629631012
flag: The letter names only “Prof. J. Tufts.” The identification with James Arthur Tufts rests on the town and on his post at Phillips Exeter Academy in 1889. Note: Pending further work.

title: Letter of William A. Bancroft, Cambridge, 3 November 1903
text: Written from Arborcroft, Ware Street, Cambridge, to “My Dear Tufts”: “We send you our deepest sympathy and hope that Mrs Tufts is not seriously injured.” It is one of three letters of condolence of November and December 1903 that are offered on eBay by one seller (asking $203.06 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 117468320868

title: Letter of Marshall Snow, Washington University, St. Louis, 9 November 1903
text: Addressed to “Dear Mr. Tufts” and written on Washington University paper, it begins: “I have just heard of the great sorrow that has come to your household.” Offered on eBay (asking $128.60 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 206731391595

title: Letter of Pitts Duffield, Fox, Duffield & Company, New York, December 1903
text: Written on the letterhead of the publishers Fox, Duffield & Company to “My dear Mr. Tufts.” As far as the photograph can be read, the writer has learned of the family’s loss through the News-Letter and mentions a daughter. The listing dates it 14 December; the dateline on the photograph appears to read the 8th. Offered on eBay (asking $248.19 on 28 November 2026).
lic: Photograph © the seller or auction house; shown with credit for research
label: eBay listing 117468320912
flag: The three 1903 letters: the eBay titles give them to “Dr. James H. Tufts,” “Philosopher James H Tufts” and “Prof. Albert Tufts,” and the letters themselves say only “Tufts.” They are placed here because the Bancroft letter of 3 November hopes that “Mrs Tufts” is not seriously injured, one day after the accident that killed Effie Miriam Tufts, and the Duffield letter appears to cite the News-Letter. The photographs do not name the addressee, and the 8th or 14th of December for the Duffield letter has not been settled. Note: Pending further work.
